spans.text: TRVM
A correct, packed-word WebAssembly reducer for the Interaction Calculus — the calculus
HVM3/HVM4 implement. Single-net reduction is schedule-independent by confluence; the
boundary-port discipline extends that to coordination-free reduction
across machines
, with no locks and no consensus. On a Wasm substrate the same runtime runs in any browser
with no server.
The IC32 runtime
Terms packed into 64-bit words over a flat heap, in C, compiling cleanly to a 9.9 KB
.wasm
module. Floating dups, in-place substitution, size-classed free-list GC.
~22–34 M interactions/s native; bit-identical results across Python reference, C native,
and Wasm builds.
The arc
ic_ref.py — correct reference reducer (fixes the higher-order-dup bug class)
ic_float.py — general reducer with floating dups; the oracle
ic32.c — packed-word native runtime (optimal sharing, self-validating)
ic32.wasm — WebAssembly build (9.9 KB, bit-identical to reference)
swarm.js — ic32.wasm coordination-free across real isolated workers (capstone)
Reproduce

blocks.text:
make test                              # the whole battery
gcc -O2 -o ic32 runtime/c/ic32.c       # native build
echo 'λx.x' | ./ic32
bash runtime/wasm/build.sh             # Wasm build
node runtime/js/swarm.js               # coordination-free across workers

spans.text: No parallel speedup is demonstrated. Every distribution result is coordination-free correct, not faster. Speedup needs the autonomous regime.
